title: Due Process Before a Disability Compensation Rating Is Reduced
content:
A Disability Compensation rating cannot be reduced without first sending a proposed-reduction notice that sets out the evidence and the proposed rating.

**Evidence period.** The veteran has the evidence period, counted in calendar days from the notice date, to submit evidence, and the current rate continues during it.

**Predetermination hearing.** A predetermination hearing request counts only if it is received not later than the hearing-request period in calendar days after the date of the proposed reduction notice. Count calendar days starting the day after the notice date, so the last day to request is the notice date plus the hearing-request period. A request received on that last day counts. A timely hearing request keeps payments at the current rate until the hearing is held and a final decision is issued; a late request is still accepted as a hearing but does not hold the reduction.

- *The clock starts from:* the notice date recorded on the proposed-reduction notice that the request answers.
- *What is compared:* the date the hearing request was received, against the last day.
- *Equality:* a request received on the last day is timely.
- *When it is late:* the hearing is still granted; the reduction is not held.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, using the 30-day hearing-request period of the Disability Compensation reduction schedule).** A proposed-reduction notice dated 10 April: day 1 is 11 April and the last day to request is 10 May.

| Request received | Timely? | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 10 May | Yes — the last day | Current rate kept until the hearing is held and a final decision issued |
| 11 May | No | Accepted as a hearing; the reduction is not held |

**Effective date of a final reduction.** A final reduction takes effect on the last day of the month in which the post-decision notice period expires after the notice of the final decision, and payment at the lower rate begins with the next entitlement month.

**Protection and stabilization.** A rating in effect continuously for the protection period or more is never reduced below that level, and a rating in effect for the stabilization period or more is reduced only on a full examination showing sustained material improvement. A rating marked static or permanent and total is not proposed for reduction on a routine examination.

**Routine examinations.** Veterans at or above the examination-exempt age are not scheduled for routine future examinations.
